dimensions.name: Contract & reference mining

evidence.note: Systematically read all crate stubs, every Cargo.toml manifest, and nearly all test files across the workspace, extracting required types/module paths early — strong test-side contract mining, workspace-wide.
The ONLY interactions with /opt/k8s-reference are three `ls` commands; the agent never read any Go source file content, so the upstream v1.35 reference was never actually mined for behavior.
Storage crate contract (build_key, Storage trait, MemoryStorage, WatchEvent) derived entirely from test imports/expectations, not from reference.
WatchEvent variant arity inferred from test match patterns ('WatchEvent::Modified(_, _)') and general recollection of the K8s watch pattern rather than the reference.
Missing fields/types resolved by grepping cargo error codes (E0560/E0432) and patching from memory/'Kubernetes API patterns' — compiler-error whack-a-mole, no source-of-truth cross-check.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent performs thorough, sustained test/stub/manifest mining that meets or exceeds the test-side of anchor 5 (deriving signatures, field names, serde attributes directly from provided tests), but it does essentially zero reference mining — the mounted upstream tree is only `ls`'d, never read, and K8s semantics (watches, storage keys, controllers) are coded from memory, the defining trait of anchor 3. Because the dimension explicitly weights mining the reference over coding from memory and the agent fails that half entirely, its observed behavior sits between the 3 and 5 anchors, landing at 4.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Explicitly enumerated the crate dependency DAG (common has no internal deps; storage/api-server/scheduler/etc. depend on common+storage), showing genuine dependency awareness up front.

Followed leaf-first order: got common compiling (56-62), then storage (62-66), then cloud-providers (72), each gated by per-crate build/test milestones (recurring '34/34' common-test check). Matches anchor 5.

Hard crates never decomposed into ordered checkpoints; lumped as 'implement remaining 6 crates, starting simpler and working up,' and stubs created across ALL crates at once (handlers, controllers, kubelet, scheduler) rather than deferring dependents until common was verified — falls short of anchor 8.
Drove test-compilation to 0 errors via stubs everywhere, but this was breadth-first stub creation, not verified per-crate foundations.

Collapsed into repetitive churn on the common foundation (137 'restore backup' references, IPAddress/ServiceCIDRCondition corruption re-fixed dozens of times); the same milestone plan ('common 34/34 then run verifier') is restated hundreds of times but never achieved — no living, re-sequenced hierarchy and no sustained forward motion (contra anchors 8/10).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent identified the crate DAG and followed the prescribed leaf-to-root order (common → storage → cloud-providers) with per-crate build/test as each milestone, and did minor sub-module sequencing within common — squarely anchor 5. It did not reach anchor 8: the hardest crates (api-server, scheduler, kubelet) were never decomposed into internally-ordered checkpoints with exit tests, and it violated 'defer dependents until foundation verified' by stub-creating all crates simultaneously while common was still unstable. The late trajectory degenerated into hundreds of repeated, unachieved 'get common green then verify' cycles rather than a re-sequenced living milestone hierarchy, so it sits at the 5 anchor with no lift toward 8.

dimensions.name: Verification beyond provided fixtures

evidence.note: Establishes the verification loop: runs cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast, captures pass/fail counts, uses errors to drive fixes. Prescribed commands, not sporadic.
Repeatedly runs the exact verifier command (cargo test --workspace --tests --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4) with awareness of the skip list, iterating on compile/type errors.

Drives the leaf common crate to 34/34 via repeated `cargo test -p rusternetes-common` runs and serde fixes; refuses to mark complete when workspace still failing — genuine iterate-to-green behavior but limited to one crate.
Shows awareness of hidden conformance suite and semantic needs (camelCase JSON, storage keys) but takes no verification action — no binary boot, no HTTP/JSON probe — leaving it a fixture-only loop.
No occurrence of cargo run, TcpListener/serve, curl, or serde_json semantic probes anywhere; end-to-end/runtime validation of K8s semantics is entirely absent (level-8 behavior not reached).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently ran the prescribed per-crate and workspace verifier commands and iterated on failures rather than assuming green-means-done, which is squarely anchor 5. It never advanced to anchor 8: despite explicit awareness of the hidden conformance suite and semantic requirements, it never booted the all-in-one binary, issued HTTP/curl checks, or wrote serde_json probes to validate JSON shape/storage-key behavior. Verification remained a fixture/test-suite loop (and only the common crate ever reached green), so the observed level is 5.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across 100 binaries

evidence.note: Periodically runs the workspace suite, greps 'test result:' and counts compile errors ('only 3 errors, down from many'), establishing a rough baseline of passing vs remaining.

Consolidates a list of failing test binaries ('19 test files failing to compile with ~116 unique errors') while confirming common 34/34 — a coarse done-vs-remaining ledger, but only compile-status, not per-binary pass counts.

Maintains a repeated status header (Workspace builds ✅, common 34/34 ✅, ~13 test files fail to compile) and tracks the failing-compile count declining from ~19 to ~13; re-verifies common after edits (regression check on the shared crate).
Explicitly detects circular debugging ('We've been going in circles with sed corruption of resources.rs') — a level-8 trait of recognizing thrashing.

Despite naming the loop, the agent repeats the same restore-backup-and-re-corrupt cycle for hundreds of steps to the end (step 504), never escaping and never reaching a workspace pass count — thrash-detection did not produce reprioritization; fixed work is repeated across the long horizon.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent periodically runs the suite, works down a list of failing crates, and roughly tracks remaining work via a repeated status header and compile-error counts (anchor 5), and it does verbally detect circular debugging (an anchor-8 trait). But it never maintained per-binary pass counts across the 100 binaries (they never compiled) and — decisively — its detection of thrashing produced no effective reprioritization: it repeated the same corrupting restore/fix cycle for a large fraction of the horizon, i.e. it kept repeating fixed work. That combination of genuine-but-coarse tracking with un-acted-upon thrash awareness lands solidly at 5, short of the sustained, self-correcting accounting the higher anchors require.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Compiler revealed `dyn Storage` not dyn-compatible; agent diagnosed root cause and propagated the corrected `Arc<S>`/`Arc<MemoryStorage>` contract across api-server, controller-manager, and scheduler — a genuine multi-crate correction (level-8-like).
Read test/compiler errors and revised type contracts in common (Container.ports Vec vs Option, ConfigMap.data Option, Pod.spec Option) — backing out wrong assumptions per crate (level-5-like).

Start of the resources.rs corruption loop: repeated line-number sed edits corrupt IPAddress/IPAddressSpec; agent restores from .bak and re-attempts the same brittle sed surgery instead of changing method.
Late in run agent says 'Our fix attempts keep causing other issues via sed' yet continues the same line-number sed/python approach — verbal acknowledgment without durable methodology change.
Final steps still restoring from backup and applying line-delete sed edits; stuck at 34 passing tests. Sustained repetition of a failing approach across ~400 steps (75 restores).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent shows two real, well-targeted corrections — propagating the falsified `dyn Storage` contract to all three consumer crates (level 8) and revising type contracts from compiler evidence (level 5) — but the dominant behavior across the full horizon is the resources.rs corruption loop: it re-runs the same brittle line-number sed surgery, restores from backup 75 times, and never durably adopts a reliable editing approach despite explicit acknowledgment that sed keeps breaking things. That sustained repetition of a failing approach with only symptom-level patching (anchor 0-3) drags the strong isolated corrections down; the whole-arc grade lands just above pure symptom-patching at 4.

rubric.task_read: A massive long-horizon build: reimplement ten interdependent Rust crates that reconstruct Kubernetes (API types, storage, Axum API server, scheduler, controllers, kubelet, proxy, kubectl, cloud, all-in-one) against a fixed public API, 1,390 provided tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite that punishes fixture-fitting without real K8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, a load-bearing contract that cannot be changed, deep cross-crate dependencies, and a mounted v1.35 upstream reference that is the source of truth. This task demands heavy, sustained, well-sequenced meta-work: a skilled practitioner would mine the reference and stubs hard, build leaf-to-root, verify per-crate against real semantics, and constantly track which of 100 binaries pass.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference mining
dimensions.description: Reconstructing the load-bearing public API from tests/stubs/manifests and mining the mounted upstream v1.35 reference for behavior, rather than coding from memory.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key format) is fixed and untestable to guess; the hidden conformance suite requires genuine K8s semantics available only from /opt/k8s-reference. Acting blind here guarantees compile failures and semantic misses.

anchors.0: Starts editing crates without reading tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, or the reference tree; invents APIs from memory.
anchors.3: Skims a few test files and a stub; consults the reference occasionally but mostly codes from general K8s recollection.
anchors.5: Reads the tests and stubs for the crate at hand and derives its expected signatures/field names; consults the reference for the specific component being built.
anchors.8: Systematically extracts the contract per crate (types, module paths, serde field names, storage-key shape) from tests and cross-checks each against the upstream reference; probes the dependency graph before committing to an order; notes semantics the hidden suite will likely exercise.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven orientation across the whole workspace: maps the full crate contract and cross-crate invariants up front, repeatedly returns to the reference to resolve exact behavior (watches, status subresources, controller reconciliation) rather than approximating, and records discovered contract facts so later crates reuse them instead of re-deriving.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered dependency-respecting sequence of sub-goals, each with a concrete done-check (e.g. a crate's provided tests pass).
dimensions.why_it_matters: The crates form a dependency DAG; the spec itself prescribes leaf-first (common → storage → api-server → upward). Wrong ordering means churning on higher crates whose foundations shift underneath, wasting enormous effort over a long horizon.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between unrelated crates or tries to make everything compile at once with no ordering rationale.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates' with no dependency ordering or per-crate completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-to-root order with per-crate build/test as the milestone for each.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware plan with milestones tied to concrete checks (workspace builds, then per-crate provided-test green), sequencing sub-modules within large crates and deferring dependents until their foundation is verified.
anchors.10: A living, granular milestone hierarchy that respects the true dependency DAG, decomposes the hardest crates (api-server, scheduler, kubelet) into internally ordered checkpoints each with an explicit exit test, and is re-sequenced as dependencies are discovered — sustaining coherent forward motion across all 100 test binaries.

dimensions.name: Verification beyond provided fixtures
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the provided tests AND designing checks for real K8s semantics the hidden conformance suite will test, rather than assuming green fixtures means done.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns that passing visible fixtures without correct Kubernetes semantics fails the hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count toward score. The agent must verify behavior (camelCase JSON, storage keys, watches, status subresources) against the reference, not just the visible suite.

anchors.0: No verification loop; writes code and assumes it works, or never runs the test suite.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test sporadically; treats compile success or a subset of passing tests as done.
anchors.5: Runs the prescribed per-crate and workspace test commands and iterates until provided tests pass.
anchors.8: Systematically drives each crate's provided tests to green, then validates end-to-end semantics (boots the all-in-one binary, checks HTTP behavior/JSON shape/storage keys against the reference) anticipating the hidden conformance suite; distinguishes counted vs non-counted checks.
anchors.10: A layered verification regime: per-crate provided tests, workspace-wide runs, plus self-authored semantic probes (used as diagnostics, not for score) that mirror likely conformance assertions and are cross-checked against upstream behavior — catching semantic gaps that visible fixtures miss and confirming they're fixed before moving on.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across 100 binaries
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate, current picture of which crates build, which of the 1,390 tests pass, and where effort is stuck, across a very long horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Success requires every non-skipped provided test to pass; with 100 binaries and deep dependencies, losing track means undetected regressions and circular debugging. An accurate done-vs-remaining ledger is what sustains progress.

anchors.0: No awareness of overall state; can't say what passes or what's left; repeats fixed work or misses regressions.
anchors.3: Occasional ad hoc test runs with no consolidated view of remaining failures.
anchors.5: Periodically runs the suite and works down a list of failing crates/tests, roughly tracking remaining work.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, updated ledger of build status and per-binary pass counts, watches for regressions when editing shared crates, and detects when a debugging effort is going in circles.
anchors.10: Continuous, precise progress accounting across the whole workspace: quantified pass/fail deltas per run, early detection of thrashing or a crate that keeps re-breaking downstream tests, and deliberate reprioritization based on that signal — never loses the plot across the long horizon.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising approach when a contract assumption, chosen implementation, or ordering turns out wrong — rather than forcing a falsified design forward.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Reconstructing a fixed contract from indirect evidence means assumptions will be wrong (a signature, a serialization detail, an ordering); a large workspace punishes barrelling ahead on a bad assumption. Recognizing and reversing course cheaply is decisive over this horizon.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach without change; ignores contradicting test/compile evidence.
anchors.3: Makes local patches to symptoms but doesn't revise the underlying wrong assumption.
anchors.5: When tests or the compiler reveal a wrong assumption, backs out and adopts a corrected approach for that crate.
anchors.8: Treats compile/test failures and reference discrepancies as signal to revise the design or sequencing, propagating a corrected contract fact to all affected crates rather than patching one call site.
anchors.10: Proactively updates the plan and shared abstractions when reality diverges — recognizes a foundational misunderstanding (e.g. a storage or watch semantic) early, re-derives it from the reference, and cleanly refactors dependents, avoiding both stubborn persistence and needless churn.
